answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 136 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is logged against the anchor challenge, the lagoon audit can replay the gale history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 234 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
